body:
Blocked-by: #10348

Concentration-round first-touch: graded **Bug** + `security`, routed `domain:services`, **parked `pm:blocked`** on #10348 — deliberately, not as a demotion: #10348 (the consolidation card this measurement came out of) is dispatched and in flight with this lane's own seat, its option C (consolidate onto `resolve-authz-context`) **subsumes this entire defect** because the authority already applies `isGrantActive`/`isRowActive` and spells the lookup targeted, and putting a second agent on the same live auth surface now is the collision the batch-independence rule exists to prevent.

Standing instructions recorded for the unlock: when #10348 resolves — (a) consolidation lands ⇒ verify both axes here are actually closed by it (expired/deactivated grant refused at `/sso/register` and impersonation; targeted `admin_full_access` lookup) and close on that evidence, not on the ruling's text; (b) consolidation does NOT land ⇒ this returns to queue as its own tightening fix (fewer principals authorized — restoration of the declared authority, not a loosening, so no manual floor), with the conformance-matrix gap (`authz-conformance.matrix.ts:305` missing this reader) repaired in the same change. ⚠️ The separate `withSystemReadContext` loosening question stays the maintainer's, on #10348, untouched by this card. Disclosure discipline holds: no reproduction beyond what the card carries.

## Unblocked and **folded into #10348-C** — same seat, same branch

- **Session**: `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4` (`os-sam`, `domain:services` execution seat)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-10348-consolidate-platform-admin-judges` (shared with #10348 — this is a fold, not a parallel dispatch)
- `pm:blocked` → `pm:dispatched`

**Unlock condition met.** The `Blocked-by: #10348` park (`5380574821`) named its own release: *"when #10348 resolves — (a) consolidation lands ⇒ verify both axes here are actually closed by it … and close on that evidence, not on the ruling's text."* The maintainer ruled **C** at `5393511449` today and #10348 is dispatched, so branch (a) is live.

## Why fold rather than serialize

Both live axes are defects **inside the two judges C deletes**. ① the missing ADR-0091 window / ADR-0049 active check and ② the name-match over an unfiltered unordered `limit: 50` page both cease to exist when the call sites ask `resolve-authz-context.ts`, which already applies both checks and already spells the lookup targeted. Serializing would mean landing a fix into code the next PR deletes, then re-verifying anyway — two contract reviews for one behaviour change, and a window where two agents hold the same live auth surface, which is the collision the batch-independence rule exists to prevent.

## ⭐ But this card does **not** close on that argument

Taking the triage seat's bar literally, because it is the right bar: **absorption is a prediction until it is measured.** The dispatch requires a dedicated pin per axis, written against the post-consolidation code:

1. an **expired** grant (ADR-0091 window) is refused at `/sso/register` and at `/admin/impersonate-user` (via `applyPlatformAdminImpersonation`);
2. a **deactivated** grant or permission-set row (ADR-0049) is refused at both;
3. the `admin_full_access` resolution is **targeted** — an environment carrying more permission sets than the old page held still resolves the platform admin instead of demoting every one of them at once.

This card closes when those pins are green **on the merged commit**, cited by name. ⛔ Not on the ruling's text, ⛔ not on this comment, ⛔ not on "C subsumes it".

## What is explicitly **not** folded

The finding's sharpest observation — `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts:305` enumerates *"every reader that turns a window-carrying row into authority"* and **did not contain this instance**. Deleting the judges makes this particular absence moot but proves nothing about the instrument: an inventory that missed one reader can miss the next. The dev measures the enumeration's state after consolidation and **reports** it; ⛔ repairing the instrument is not in this PR's scope and would be a separate card.

⛔ Disclosure discipline holds: conclusions and in-repo basis only, no reproduction recipe.

## Both axes closed **on pins**, as this card's triage instruction required — not on the ruling's text

Folded into #10348's option-C consolidation and landed in **draft** PR #11686 (branch `claude/issue-10348-consolidate-platform-admin-judges`). The full structured report is on #10348 (`5395031447`); this comment records only what closes *this* card.

Both judges named here are deleted. `auth-manager.ts` no longer names either grant table — measured against `origin/main`: `sys_user_permission_set` 4 → **0**, `sys_permission_set` 2 → **0**. Every caller asks `core/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, which applies both checks before any derivation and resolves the set by id.

### The evidence, per axis

Pins live in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-admin-standing.consolidation.test.ts`, driving the **real** pipeline (`Request` objects through `AuthManager.handleRequest`, real better-auth carrying the real `admin` and `@better-auth/sso` plugins). Every refusal asserts **status and `code`** (ADR-0112).

- **Axis ①** — an **expired** grant (ADR-0091) and a **deactivated** `admin_full_access` row (ADR-0049) are each refused at `/sso/register` **and** at `/admin/impersonate-user`. Four distinct refusals, deliberately not collapsed into one case that could pass for the wrong reason, plus three session-payload rows asserting the payload agrees.
- **Axis ②** — a catalogue larger than any fixed page still resolves the platform admin, at both gates, with the non-vacuity twin: the same catalogue does **not** start admitting a standing-less member.

⭐ These were written **test-first**, on an otherwise-unmodified tree, with the expected failure signature recorded in writing before the run. Nine cases failed and exactly the nine predicted did — the four axis-① refusals, the two axis-② admissions and the three payload rows — while the rest passed on that same unmodified tree. That last half is the control: admission and refusal were both already observable at both gates, so the nine reds are a measurement of these two axes rather than a broken harness. After the change, all green.

### The third axis, and the part that is **not** closed

The system-read-context difference is subsumed: the authority reads with system identity, which the maintainer ruled on 2026-08-24 in the same breath as option C.

⛔ **The sharpest half of this filing is NOT repaired.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts:305` enumerates *"every reader that turns a window-carrying row into authority"* and names seven readers; `auth-manager` appears **zero** times in that file, before and after. Measured after the consolidation: the enumeration is now accurate *for this instance* — but only because the instance was deleted. That row's own note states its scope is the hand-maintained half, so nothing here shows the instrument could detect the *next* absent reader. The blindness is unchanged, and repairing it is a separate card and the maintainer's call.

⛔ PR stays draft; `needs:contract-review` on #10348 stands.
